A galvanometer of resistance $100\ \Omega$ when connected in series with $400\ \Omega$ measures a voltage of upto $10\ \mathrm{V}$. The value of resistance required to convert the galvanometer into ammeter to read upto $10\ \mathrm{A}$ is $x \times 10^{-2}\ \Omega$. The value of $x$ is :
questions.solution:
$i_g = \frac{10}{400+100} = 20 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{A}$
For ammeter
Let shunt resistance $= S$
$i_gR = (i - i_g)S$
$20 \times 10^{-3} \times 100 = 10\,S$
$S = 20 \times 10^{-2}\ \Omega$

questions.stem: The vehicles carrying inflammable fluids usually have metallic chains touching the ground :

To protect tyres from catching dirt from ground.

questions.stem: If n is the number density and d is the diameter of the molecule, then the average distance covered by a molecule between two successive collisions (i.e. mean free path) is represented by :

d = diameter of the molecule
$\lambda = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}\,\pi d^{2}n}$  (By Theory)

questions.stem: A particle moves in x-y plane under the influence of a force $\vec{F}$ such that its linear momentum is $\vec{P}(t) = \hat{i}\cos(kt) - \hat{j}\sin(kt)$. If $k$ is constant, the angle between $\vec{F}$ and $\vec{P}$ will be :
questions.solution:
$\vec{P} = \cos(kt)\hat{i} - \sin(kt)\hat{j}$ ; $|\vec{P}| = 1$
$\because\ \vec{P} = m\vec{v}$
$\therefore\ \hat{P} = \hat{v}$
$\Rightarrow \hat{v} = \cos(kt)\hat{i} - \sin(kt)\hat{j}$
$\hat{a} = \frac{-k\sin(kt)\hat{i} - k\cos(kt)\hat{j}}{k}$
$\Rightarrow \hat{a} = -\sin kt\,\hat{i} - \cos kt\,\hat{j}$
$\because\ \hat{F} = \hat{a} = -\sin kt\,\hat{i} - \cos kt\,\hat{j}$
$\cos\theta = \frac{\hat{F}\cdot\hat{P}}{|\hat{F}||\hat{P}|} = -\frac{\sin kt\cos kt + \sin kt\cos kt}{1 \times 1} = 0$
$\Rightarrow \theta = \frac{\pi}{2}$

A series LCR circuit is subjected to an AC signal of 200 V, 50 Hz. If the voltage across the inductor ($L = 10\ \mathrm{mH}$) is 31.4 V, then the current in this circuit is ________ :
questions.solution:
Voltage across inductor $V_L = IX_L$
$31.4 = I[L\omega]$
$31.4 = I[L(2\pi f)]$
$31.4 = I[10 \times 10^{-3}(2 \times 3.14)] \times 50$
$\Rightarrow I = 10\ \mathrm{A}$

questions.stem: What is the dimensional formula of $ab^{-1}$ in the equation $\left(P + \frac{a}{V^{2}}\right)(V - b) = RT$, where letters have their usual meaning.
The output (Y) of logic circuit given below is 0 only when :
A body is moving unidirectionally under the influence of a constant power source. Its displacement in time t is proportional to :
questions.solution:
$P = \text{constant} \Rightarrow FV = \text{constant}$
$\Rightarrow m\frac{dV}{dt}V = \text{constant}$
$\int_{0}^{V} V\,dV = (C)\int_{0}^{t} dt$
$\left(\frac{V^{2}}{2}\right) = Ct$
$V \propto t^{1/2}$
$\frac{ds}{dt} \propto t^{1/2}$
$\int_{0}^{S} ds = K\int_{0}^{t} t^{1/2}\,dt$
$S = K \times \frac{2}{3}t^{3/2}$
$S \propto t^{3/2}$
$\therefore$ displacement is proportional to $(t)^{3/2}$

questions.stem: During an adiabatic process, if the pressure of a gas is found to be proportional to the cube of its absolute temperature, then the ratio of $\frac{C_P}{C_V}$ for the gas is :
questions.solution:
$P \propto T^{3}$
$PT^{-3} = \text{constant}$
$\because\ \frac{PV}{T} = nR = \text{constant}$ from ideal gas equation
$(P)(PV)^{-3} = \text{constant}$
$P^{-2}V^{-3} = \text{constant}$  ...(1)
$\because$ Process equation for adiabatic process is
$PV^{\gamma} = \text{constant}$  ...(2)
Comparing equation (1) and (2)
$\frac{C_P}{C_V} = \gamma = \frac{3}{2}$

A solenoid of length 0.5 m has a radius of 1 cm and is made up of 'm' number of turns. It carries a current of 5A. If the magnitude of the magnetic field inside the solenoid is $6.28 \times 10^{-3}$ T, then the value of m is :
questions.solution:
$\mu_0ni = B$   $n$ = number of turns per unit length
$\mu_0\left(\frac{m}{\ell}\right)i = B$
$m = \frac{B.\ell}{\mu_0 i} = \frac{6.28 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.5}{12.56 \times 10^{-7} \times 5}$
$m = 500$

questions.stem: The shortest wavelength of the spectral lines in the Lyman series of hydrogen spectrum is 915 Å. The longest wavelength of spectral lines in the Balmer series will be _______ Å.
questions.solution:
Lyman Series
Shortest, $\frac{hc}{\lambda} = -13.6\left(\frac{1}{n_1^{2}} - \frac{1}{n_2^{2}}\right)$
$\lambda\downarrow\ E\uparrow$ ; $\frac{hc}{\lambda_0} = -13.6(1)$
Balmer Series :
$\frac{hc}{\lambda_1} = -13.6\left(\frac{1}{2^{2}} - \frac{1}{3^{2}}\right)$
$\frac{hc}{\lambda_1} = -13.6\left(\frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{9}\right)$
$\frac{hc}{\lambda_1} = -13.6 \times \left(\frac{5}{36}\right)$
$\Rightarrow \frac{-13.6\lambda_0}{\lambda_1} = -13.6 \times \frac{5}{36}$
$\lambda_1 = \frac{\lambda_0 \times 36}{5} = \frac{915 \times 36}{5} = 6588$
